story: I paid Rs 6,00,000 to a modular kitchen company in Bengaluru on 1 June 2026. They never installed it and refuse to refund. I have the invoice and bank transfer receipt.

timeline.event: Paid Rs 6,00,000 to modular kitchen company in Bengaluru

facts.user_goal: Get a refund of Rs 6,00,000 for a modular kitchen that was never installed.

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 01 Jun 2028 (571 days left). This counts 2 years from 01 Jun 2026 (your purchase date - counted from the earliest possible day, to be safe). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.

facts_used.start_basis: purchase date (earliest possible start, to be safe)

rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 600,000, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with a Rs 200 fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

answer.summary: You paid Rs 6,00,000 for a modular kitchen that was never installed. The company refusing to refund is an unfair trade practice. You can file a complaint in the District Consumer Commission in Bengaluru.

claims.text: A consumer is any person who buys goods for a consideration that has been paid, and a modular kitchen for your home is for personal use, not business.
Refusing to take back or withdraw defective goods and refund the consideration within 30 days is an unfair trade practice.
The District Commission has jurisdiction to hear your complaint because you paid Rs 6,00,000.
You must file your complaint within two years of 1 June 2026. You have until 1 June 2028.

next_steps.action: Call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915 to complain and ask for a refund.
next_steps.why: This is a free first step to try to resolve the issue directly with the company.

next_steps.action: Send a written complaint to the company's grievance officer demanding a refund.
next_steps.why: This creates a paper trail proving you asked for your money back before going to court.

next_steps.why: You paid Rs 6,00,000, so the fee is only Rs 200 and you do not need a lawyer.

draft:
Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for refund

On 01 June 2026 I paid Rs 600,000 to you for [FILL: product/service and order number]. [FILL: what went wrong, e.g. product defective / service not provided]. Despite my requests you have not refunded the amount.

I request a full refund of Rs 600,000 within 15 days of receiving this letter.

If the refund is not made, I intend to file a complaint before the District Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: Invoice, Bank transfer receipt.

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]
escalation_reasons: support check unavailable for some sentences (treated as not confirmed)
draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
